gen-flavors-gf-anek-latin: Anek Latin stands tall in its lowercase, nearly meeting the capitals, with rounds left open instead of curled shut. Flavors, the whimsical display heading above it, draws every letter like pipe cleaner.
gen-flavors-gf-anek-malayalam: Anek Malayalam keeps its lowercase close to cap height, with curves whose tips never touch. Beside it, Flavors is a loud display heading whose strokes carry no hairlines at all, only sturdy weight.
gen-flavors-gf-anek-odia: Anek Odia has rounds that stay unsealed, like an unlatched hook, and capitals barely above the lowercase. And Flavors, a thread of ink with no swelling or tapering, gives that quiet sans-serif a playful, commanding neighbor.
gen-flavors-gf-anek-tamil: Whimsical and a bit commanding, Flavors draws its curves without any pinching. Anek Tamil answers with big round lowercase bowls, and its c and s look half unwrapped.
gen-flavors-gf-anek-telugu: Anek Telugu reads in wide, tall bowls and unlatched rounds. Flavors does the shouting, its w showing no thick or thin strokes, while the sans-serif body does the quiet, steady talking underneath.
gen-flavors-gf-anuphan: Big round lowercase bowls and open curves with clear gaps give Anuphan a friendly, unhurried way of reading. Flavors keeps its stroke widths constant from stem to curve.
gen-flavors-gf-arimo: Arimo reads with a tall mean line and generous gaps at the ends of its rounded letters. Arimo then sits quietly under Flavors, whose curves and straights share one line width, so the display heading gets the spotlight.
gen-flavors-gf-armata: Armata reads spaciously, with room between characters and lowercase bodies filling most of the letter height. And Flavors, with its line like spaghetti laid out in letters, adds the whimsy that the sans leaves out.
gen-flavors-gf-athiti: Approachable and contemporary, Athiti has a gap you can see through in each s and a mean line set high. And Athiti is the one to enlarge if the text needs more room, never Flavors.
gen-flavors-gf-atkinson-hyperlegible: Flavors brings whimsy with diagonals as heavy as its stems, and no thick-thin swell like a pointed brush. Atkinson Hyperlegible reads approachably, with wide-set terminals on s, though its ascenders and capitals feel clipped.
